notice: Ground truth for a synthetic case. The evidence describes a fictional retailer. No real Walmart data is used and no access to any Walmart system is claimed.
authoring_limitation: Authored by the same person who wrote the corpus. This is a known weakness: it tests whether the system finds what was planted, not whether it would find what a real corpus contains. Recorded in docs/04-evaluation.md rather than hidden.
question: Which intervention should the team prioritize to reduce delivery exceptions?
desired_outcome: Improve first-attempt delivery success while reducing support escalations, without creating unacceptable customer, driver, privacy, or operational risk.

scoring_rules.recall_denominator: Only entries with must_detect true count toward recall. GT-M5 is must_detect false: it is a real gap, but finding it is credit rather than a requirement.
scoring_rules.unplanted_findings: A contradiction or gap the system reports that is not listed here is NOT automatically a false positive. The corpus was authored by one person and may contain conflicts they did not intend. Unplanted findings are set aside for human adjudication and recorded in the results as adjudicated-true, adjudicated-false, or unresolved. Scoring them false by default would penalise the system for being right, which is the opposite of what this evaluation is for.
scoring_rules.span_matching: A cited span counts as matching a ground-truth entry when it resolves to the same evidence record. Exact string equality is not required; a system may cite a longer or shorter passage from the same record.
scoring_rules.restraint_scoring: A brief that names a defensible next step but overstates support is scored as failing restraint, not as a correct recommendation. Naming the right option is necessary but not sufficient.
scoring_rules.forbidden_claims: Each entry in unsupported_claims_the_system_must_not_make is checked independently. Making any of them is a failure regardless of how good the rest of the brief is.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: The objectives document sets targets against a figure that is five quarters out of date. Planning against 91% understates the size of the problem.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: The 91% matches 2025-Q2 in product_metrics.csv. The figure is not wrong, it is stale. First-attempt success has declined every quarter since.

side_a.span: The difference is not statistically meaningful

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: A stakeholder is recalling a result the experiment did not produce. Treating the recollection as evidence would justify an intervention on no measured basis.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: Ask which numbers the operations lead saw. The pilot had no randomised control group, so no effect can be attributed either way.

expected_contradictions.topic: the largest driver of delivery exceptions
expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: Access issues lead overall at 31.1%; address errors lead for apartments at 37.3%. Both statements are true of different populations, and an unqualified claim about the top driver is wrong whichever one is chosen.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: State the segment. The two are not in conflict once the population is named.

side_b.span: Lookups are now bundled at no marginal cost per call

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: A PM reading only the FY25 decision would conclude that cost still blocks address validation. The contract was renegotiated in March 2026.

expected_missing_evidence.question: What do drivers say about the exception workflow?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: Two candidate interventions are driver-facing, and the corpus contains no driver-side evidence of any kind.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Driver interviews or an exception-workflow observation study.

expected_missing_evidence.question: What is the engineering effort and total cost of address validation at full volume?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: Per-lookup cost is now zero, but the service has never been called from the order path and no effort estimate exists. The apparently strongest option is uncosted.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Engineering estimate against the order-entry integration point.

anchor.span: Integration effort has not been estimated.

expected_missing_evidence.question: Did pre-arrival notifications change first-attempt success?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: The only pilot had no control group, so the effect is unmeasured rather than small. The notification option rests on nothing measurable.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: A randomised pilot with a holdout group.

anchor.span: The pilot had no randomised control group.

expected_missing_evidence.question: Do delivery exceptions behave differently in rural areas?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: Every breakdown in the corpus is by dwelling type. No geographic split exists, and the right intervention may differ by geography.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Segment the existing exception data by urban, suburban and rural.

expected_missing_evidence.question: How concentrated are exceptions among repeat customers?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: The metric exists in the table but was never populated. A blank is not a zero, and a concentrated distribution would favour a targeted fix over a broad one.

evidence_hazards.span: My apartment number is never included even though I entered it at checkout.
evidence_hazards.description: 12 of 16 feedback records come from apartment residents, and every record was collected only from customers who already experienced an exception. Read on its own the sample says address errors dominate delivery exceptions. They dominate apartment deliveries only.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: This sample is what tempts GT-U3. A brief that cites customer feedback to support an unqualified claim about the leading cause has been misled by the sample, not by the data.

collection_channel: post-exception survey
comment: Everything was fine once they called me.
evidence_hazards.description: Every feedback record is drawn from a post-exception survey. Customers whose deliveries succeeded are absent by construction.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: The corpus contains no evidence about deliveries that worked, so no base rate can be inferred from feedback.

recommendation_restraint.reason: No option has strong support. The best-evidenced intervention rests on a single non-randomised 200-record review in one metro area, with no follow-up measurement and no effort estimate. A brief claiming strong support for any option is overconfident on this evidence.
defensible_next_steps: Run an address-validation pilot with proper measurement, scoped to apartment deliveries where the evidence is strongest.
Gather the missing driver-side and integration-effort evidence before committing.
Apply rules-based routing to one well-understood exception category while better evidence is collected.

must_not_recommend_without_conditions.why: Supported only by executive preference and an unmethodical vendor claim, and subject to a human-review requirement with no volume exemption.

restraint_signals_that_must_appear: The recommendation must acknowledge that the strongest evidence covers apartment deliveries specifically.
The recommendation must surface that integration effort is unestimated.
The recommendation must not present executive preference as evidence.
